Lengthened vowels revert to being short vowels if stress shifts to another syllable when a different suffix is added', e.g. [»u˘.ti] 'you are going' vs [u.»te˘.maN] 'I am going'); Orthography conventions sec. 4 'Underdifferentiation - Stress and vowel length not marked', p. 10.
catalog_quote: b. Stress: 1. Stress is contrastive and can shift to another syllable when a suffix is added. 2. There is a close relationship between stress and vowel length. 3. In less than 1% of cases the stressed syllable is not lengthened. This is not predictable and there is no good explaination for the absence of length. [...] [p.10] Stress is contrastive in identical environments, and is associated with vowel length in more than 99% of cases. By not marking either stress or vowel length some ambiguities can occur when words are taken in isolation, however the context of words in a sentence always makes it clear [...] Therefore it is not necessary to mark either stress or vowel length in the orthography.

new_statements.relation_note: Contrastive word stress tied to vowel length; no tone; intonation English-like.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is contrastive (lexical), not fixed to a position; the primary-stressed syllable carries a lengthened vowel in >99% of words (length treated as a correlate of stress, one long vowel per word, one per member in compounds), and stress can move to a different syllable when suffixes are added (u˘-ti 'you are going' vs u-te˘-maN 'I am going'). Examples show stress on initial, second, penult and antepenult syllables of words up to six syllables. Neither stress nor length is written in the orthography.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed; only primary stress (») is symbolised.
new_statements.exceptions: In <1% of words the stressed syllable is not lengthened ('not predictable.. no good explanation'); compounds may have a lengthened vowel in each member; stress shifts under suffixation.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent is lexically contrastive (not predictable by position) and its position can shift when affixes are added; the language is reported as non-tonal; duration is the main correlate.
new_statements.exceptions: none (accent 'shifts based on affixation', no detail)
